title: Board of Peace Announces Hamas Disarmament Roadmap After Cairo Talks — Israel Yet to Formally Accept
detail: July 28-31, 2026 — A Hamas delegation traveled to Cairo from July 28 for talks with Egyptian, Qatari, and Turkish mediators, producing what negotiators called 'rare progress.' On July 30-31, the Board of Peace announced mediators (Egypt, Qatar, Turkey, and the US) had finalized a roadmap for phased Hamas disarmament: weapons inventoried within 14 days and stored — not surrendered to Israel — under a Palestinian National Committee, with sector-by-sector demilitarization tied to phased Israeli withdrawal over an estimated 200-300 days. A seven-member executive board led by Tony Blair would oversee governance, with a roughly 5,000-strong International Stabilization Force providing security. Hamas official Ghazi Hamad said Hamas would not implement the roadmap unless Israel met its own withdrawal obligations, and Israel had not formally accepted the roadmap as of July 31.

title: RSF Commander Hemedti Vows to Retake Khartoum, Orders 'Tribal Mobilization'
detail: July 30-31, 2026 — RSF released a video of commander Mohamed Hamdan 'Hemedti' Dagalo ordering forces to seize the capital, days after SAF announced recapture of a key North Kordofan logistics corridor (the Al Sadarat highway and towns of Bara, Umm Sayala, and Jabra al-Sheikh) — its most significant territorial gain of the year. Hemedti followed on July 31 with a speech calling for 'tribal mobilization' of fighters for renewed operations toward Khartoum and Kordofan, a direct threat to the US-brokered peace proposal both sides had just formally responded to, and a signal that battlefield escalation was outpacing diplomacy.
